 Goodlife Sharvari turns disco diva as Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla bring 1970s party glamour to Art Mumbai
 By Sanjali Brahma 
 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 2:24PM | 3 min read Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla with Sharvari 
 Advertisement Disco balls, sequins, dramatic drapes and a whole lot of shimmer – Abu Jani and Sandeep Khosla brought the party to the runway with Disco Inferno, their latest fashion presentation at Art Mumbai. Held at the Mahalaxmi Racecourse on November 12, the showcase celebrated the unapologetic glamour of the 1970s and 1980s, with actor Sharvari taking centre stage as the showstopper in two striking looks.
 The designer duo, known for their maximalist approach to Indian couture, went all out with a collection that was anything but understated. Think dazzling embellishments, sheer fabrics, intricate embroidery, metallic accents and silhouettes that borrowed from vintage disco dressing while retaining a distinctly Indian sensibility. And, of course, there was Sharvari, who brought two very different moods to the runway.
 For her first appearance, the actor stepped out in a dramatic red saree-inspired ensemble. The contemporary drape featured a sweeping trail that moved with every step, paired with a heavily embellished gold-toned blouse. Intricate metallic straps and crystal detailing across the bodice added a touch of disco glamour, while the rich red fabric brought all the drama. She later returned in a dazzling, figure-hugging mini dress featuring a plunging neckline, colourful gemstones and elaborate crystal embellishments. The fringed detailing added movement to the outfit, making it quite the party-ready statement.
 Advertisement But Sharvari was hardly the only one bringing the disco fever. The menswear offering played with sheer layers, open shirts and embroidered trousers. One standout look featured a red shirt worn open at the chest, teamed with black trousers covered in vibrant floral and paisley-inspired motifs. Another model sported a black sheer shirt with a plunging neckline, paired with heavily embellished trousers that caught the light with every movement. There were also grey embroidered jackets and coordinated trousers, with intricate patterns extending to the cuffs and hems. Striped ensembles, fluid kurtas and sheer tunics added another dimension to the collection.
 The womenswear kept the glamour dialled up, too. From off-shoulder silhouettes and richly embellished skirts to vibrant colours, sequinned separates and dramatic drapes, the collection moved between contemporary party dressing and traditional Indian craftsmanship. One look paired a deep burgundy off-shoulder top with a colourful embellished mini skirt, while another brought together an olive-green ensemble and a vibrant orange drape. A black blouse teamed with a richly embroidered skirt offered another striking interpretation of evening dressing. The colour palette was just as spirited, moving from fiery reds, burnt oranges and jewel-toned greens to deep purples, midnight blacks, muted greys and shimmering metallics, with flashes of gold and silver tying the disco-inspired extravagance together.
 Advertisement The accessories deserved a moment of their own. Embellished handbags, colourful embroidered totes, crystal-studded clutches and sculptural headpieces added to the theatricality of the presentation. One particularly striking headpiece featured golden spikes radiating outwards, while another model walked the runway with a dramatic silver crystal head accessory. The bags ranged from jewel-encrusted miniatures to vibrant, artwork-like pieces that looked almost too good to be tucked away.
 And then there was the set. A giant illuminated elephant installation served as the centrepiece of the runway, with shimmering mirror discs, crystal-like hangings and ornate embellishments creating a rather spectacular entrance for the models. The elaborate structure, with its textured ivory finish and decorative details, brought an element of fantasy to the presentation. Under the runway lights, the hanging mirrors and embellishments reflected the light, adding to the disco-inspired atmosphere.
 With Disco Inferno, Abu Jani and Sandeep Khosla turned the runway into a celebration of fashion without a quiet note in sight. It was a world where mirrors became moonlight, sequins caught little pieces of the spotlight and every swish of fabric seemed to carry the rhythm of another era. Sharvari may have had the final word as showstopper, but the evening belonged to the spectacle – a glittering reminder that some fashions are not meant to fade into the background. They are meant to dance, dazzle and leave the lights on long after the music stops.
